children: Singh brings more than 24 years of HR and business leadership experience spanning talent, transformation and workforce strategy

Pavitra Singh, who has served as chief human resources officer and vice president at PepsiCo India and South Asia, has joined the board of Burma Burma Restaurant & Tea Room. The date of her joining the board has not been disclosed.

Singh brings more than 24 years of experience across human resources, talent management, organisational transformation, business strategy and engineering-led industries. Her move to Burma Burma comes as the restaurant company continues to expand its frontline and corporate workforce.
Singh spent more than 13 years at PepsiCo, where she held several HR leadership positions before becoming CHRO and vice president, PepsiCo India and South Asia, in October 2019.
In the role, she led the people agenda for PepsiCo India and South Asia, covering talent, capability building and organisational development across a large workforce.

Before becoming CHRO, Singh served as director and head of Talent Acquisition for Asia, the Middle East and North Africa. She also held the position of director, Global Campus COE, where she worked on the company’s global campus hiring strategy and leadership pipeline.

Earlier at PepsiCo, Singh headed Talent Acquisition for the India region from August 2015 to December 2017. Her responsibilities included recruitment transformation, the use of digital tools in hiring and the development of employee value propositions for India.

Across her career, Singh has worked on talent architecture, capability frameworks, industrial relations, frontline transformation and hiring ecosystems. Her experience has also included supporting organisations through restructuring and business transformation.

Singh has also been involved in initiatives focused on workforce development and employment opportunities. At PepsiCo, she was associated with RevolutioNari, a programme focused on skilling, awareness and employment opportunities for women and households.

Her professional interests include building AI-ready organisations, future skills and developing leadership capabilities. She has participated in future-of-work forums involving organisations such as SHRM, NHRDN, ET and BW.
Singh is also a member of the SHRM Advisory Council and has previously served as an independent director at SPML Infra.

At Burma Burma, Singh joins the board with experience spanning people strategy, organisational growth and workforce transformation. The appointment comes as the company works to build its teams and organisational structure alongside its wider business expansion.
Singh’s joining date and the specific responsibilities attached to her board role have not been disclosed.
